授業概要
This course introduces students to both the fundamental and advanced aspects of nanomaterials and their use in modern devices. It begins by building a basic understanding of nanotechnology, including what nanomaterials are, how they are classified, and why materials behave differently at the nanoscale.
After establishing these foundations, the course moves on to more advanced topics, focusing on how the structure of nanomaterials influences their physical, chemical, and electronic properties. Students will learn about various fabrication and characterization techniques, as well as how nanomaterials are applied in areas such as electronics, energy systems, and sensing technologies.

全体の教育目標
The goal of this course is to help students understand how nanomaterials are structured and how they are used in modern devices.
By the end of the course, students should be able to think critically about Nanotechnology concepts and gain the confidence to engage with current research in the field of Nanomaterials.
個別の教育目標
By the end of the course, students will be able to:
1. Understand the basic relationship between the structure and properties of nanomaterials
2. Describe common fabrication methods used for nanomaterials and devices
3. Explain the purpose and basic working principles of major characterization techniques
4. Discuss how nanomaterials are used in different device applications
